subject: Renewal: Twilight.ai - staged commit, spike credits, and price-hold
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@twilight.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Oct 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning and mid-Q1 spike/price concerns

Hi Rishi,

Quick note as we start planning our renewal — our execs want a predictable unit price for the next 12 months but with a safety buffer for two planned marketing spikes in Q1 and Q2. We did the numbers and expect baseline usage to increase ~40% year-over-year, with two short spikes (~48 hours) that could be 6–8x baseline.

Two asks up front:
- Can you hold current unit pricing through the renewal period if we commit to a staged uplift?
- Would Redwood consider a small pool of burst credits (or a surge-credit bucket) to cover the Q1 spike rather than fully increasing committed capacity?

I can share our usage runbook and a rough calendar. Also copying Marc (ops) who will handle procurement.

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of ML Platform, Twilight.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@twilight.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Oct 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning and mid-Q1 spike/price concerns

Hi Elaine — thanks for the heads up and the clarity on the spikes. Good news: we have a couple of approaches that trade between committed uplift + price-hold or a smaller commit + allocated surge credits.

I took a quick skim of the runbook you attached (nice detail) and looped Monica from Solutions so she can validate the spike characteristics against our autoscaling/bursting model. Before I put a formal number on things, two quick clarifying questions:
1) Are the spikes predictable windows (dates) or probabilistic? If predictable, we can design a short-term burst pool tied to those windows and price it differently.
2) Do you need hard SLA for those spikes (e.g., 99th pct latency during spikes) or just capacity availability?

I'll draft a 2-option commercial we can move to procurement on next week:
- Option A: Staged commit + price-hold (12 months) with conditional uplift tranches at +25% and +50%.
- Option B: Moderate commit + surge-credit pool (time-limited, consumed only during declared spike windows).

Sending a quick proposal draft by Wednesday.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@twilight.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Oct 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning and mid-Q1 spike/price concerns

Elaine / Rishi — quick technical note from my side after reviewing your runbook and recent telemetry (attached CSV):
- The two spike windows you described look like short, high-peak jobs rather than a long steady increase — that maps well to our burst queue.
- For latency-sensitive endpoints we advise reserving a small baseline commit for the traffic tail and using the burst pool for headroom.
- If Twilight wants to avoid an invoice delta on non-declared spikes, we recommend a declared-window model (you tell us the dates, we provision a temporary tier and bill against surge credits).

I've attached the usage breakdown and a simple sensitivity chart. Happy to jump on a 30-min call and walk through numbers.

- Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: twilight-usage.csv

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@twilight.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Nov 2028 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: staged-commit + spike-credit option (Twilight.ai renewal)

Elaine — attaching a compact commercial for the renewal with two executable options (spreadsheet attached):

Summary (short):
Option 1 — Staged Commit + 12-month price-hold
- Baseline commit: 1.4x current average (covers projected YOY growth).
- Tranche 1 (after month 3): +25% optional uplift, Tranche 2 (after month 6): +25% optional uplift.
- Applied discount: 12% on baseline tokens for the 12-month term.
- Price-hold: unit price locked for the 12-month term unless customer requests a higher-tier model.
- Rollover credits: up to 20% of unused committed tokens may roll into next billing period as one-time credits.

Option 2 — Moderate Commit + Spike Credit Pool
- Baseline commit: 1.1x current average.
- Surge-credit bucket: 200k token-equivalent credits for the 12 months to be consumed only during declared spike windows.
- Applied discount: 8% on baseline tokens.
- If declared spikes exceed the bucket, we convert overage to 'pre-negotiated overage rate' (lower than standard pay-as-you-go).

Commercial sweeteners included with both options:
- One-time onboarding credit (applied to first invoice) to offset migration tuning.
- SLA exception clause for declared spike windows (we commit to capacity and 95th pct latency target for endpoints in scope).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Pick the preferred option (A or B) and confirm declared spike windows (if B).
2) Jordan will prepare the order form and a short amendment for price-hold language.
3) Legal can run a brief review — Jordan will loop in Finance and Legal.

Attachment: TW-proposal-Nov1.xlsx

Happy to hop on a call to walk through the spreadsheet Thursday afternoon.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Park <elaine@twilight.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marc Dupree <marc.dupree@twilight.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: staged-commit + spike-credit option (Twilight.ai renewal)

Rishi — appreciate the clear options. After an internal readout we prefer Option 2 (Moderate Commit + Spike Credit Pool). Two small asks before we sign:
1) Can you increase the surge-credit bucket to 300k token-equivalents if we agree to a 6% prepayment on the baseline commit?
2) Provide a short clause in the amendment that the declared-window SLA will be effective only for windows notified at least 72 hours in advance.

If you can confirm those two items I’ll route to Procurement & Legal and Marc will push PO this week.

Elaine Park
Head of ML Platform, Twilight.ai
